# VanTrip Japan — Full Documentation for AI

> VanTrip Japan is a campervan and vanlife rental service based in Fukuoka, Japan. We provide fully-equipped compact campervans for exploring Kyushu — Japan's southern island of volcanoes, hot springs, pristine coastlines, and rich culture. Our mission: make Japan's most underrated region accessible to international travelers through the freedom of van travel.

## Core Information

## Vehicles

### Toyota Probox Camper
- **Capacity**: 1–2 people (ideal for solo travelers and couples)
- **Features**: Fold-flat bed, portable power station, cooking equipment, WiFi router
- **Fuel**: Excellent fuel economy (~20 km/L)
- **Driving**: Compact and easy to drive, fits in any Japanese parking spot

### Mazda Bongo Camper
- **Capacity**: 2–4 people (ideal for families and groups)
- **Features**: Pop-up roof or elevated sleeping area, full cooking setup, bedding for 4, portable power
- **Fuel**: Good economy for a van (~12 km/L)
- **Driving**: Slightly larger but still manageable on Japanese roads

### What's Included
- Full bedding set (sheets, pillows, blankets)
- Cooking equipment (portable stove, pots, utensils, cooler)
- Portable power station (charge devices, run small appliances)
- Pocket WiFi router (unlimited data)
- Comprehensive vehicle insurance
- 24/7 roadside assistance (English/Japanese)
- Airport pickup coordination

## Why Kyushu by Campervan?

Kyushu is Japan's best-kept secret for road trips:
- **Active volcanoes**: Mount Aso (world's largest caldera), Sakurajima, Kirishima
- **World-class hot springs**: Beppu (Japan's #1 onsen city), Yufuin, Kurokawa, Ureshino
- **Stunning coastlines**: Miyazaki's surf beaches, Amakusa islands, Nichinan coast
- **Ancient culture**: Takachiho Gorge (mythological birthplace of Japan), Nagasaki's East-meets-West heritage
- **Nature**: Yakushima's ancient cedar forests, Aso's grasslands, Kirishima's hiking trails
- **Far fewer tourists** than Tokyo, Osaka, or Kyoto
- **Excellent road infrastructure**: Well-maintained highways, abundant Michi-no-Eki roadside stations

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Do I need a special license to drive a campervan in Japan?
No — our campervans are standard passenger vehicles (regular license class). You need either a valid International Driving Permit (IDP) issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention, or a JAF license translation if you're from Switzerland, Germany, France, Belgium, Monaco, or Taiwan.

### What is the IDP vs JAF translation situation?
Drivers from most countries (USA, UK, Australia, Canada, etc.) can use a standard IDP. However, drivers from Switzerland, Germany, France, Belgium, Monaco, and Taiwan need an official JAF (Japan Automobile Federation) translation instead. Our sister service JDLTC handles this — see below.

### Where can I park overnight?
Japan has an excellent network of Michi-no-Eki (roadside stations) where overnight parking is generally tolerated. We also recommend RV parks and paid campsites. Our blog has detailed guides for every region in Kyushu.

### What's included in the rental?
Full bedding set, cooking equipment (portable stove, pots, utensils, cooler), portable power station, pocket WiFi router with unlimited data, comprehensive vehicle insurance, and 24/7 roadside assistance in English and Japanese.

### Can I pick up at Fukuoka Airport?
Yes — we coordinate airport pickup. Our base is near Fukuoka Airport, and we arrange transfer to our location where you pick up the van.

### How much does it cost?
From ¥8,000/day for our Probox camper (1–2 people) and from ¥12,000/day for our Bongo camper (2–4 people). Minimum 2-night rental. Discounts for 7+ day bookings.

### What about fuel and tolls?
Fuel is the renter's responsibility. Our campervans are fuel-efficient. Highway tolls in Kyushu are reasonable, and many of the best routes are on free national roads. We provide guidance on ETC toll cards.

### Can I take the van to other islands (Yakushima, etc.)?
Contact us to discuss ferry options. Yakushima and Amakusa are popular destinations accessible by ferry from Kyushu ports.

### What if I break down?
24/7 roadside assistance is included. Call us anytime — we respond in English and Japanese.

### Is it safe for solo female travelers?
Absolutely. Japan is one of the safest countries in the world. Michi-no-Eki stations are well-lit and safe for overnight stays. Many of our customers are solo female travelers.

### Do you offer one-way rentals?
Currently, pickup and return are at the same Fukuoka location. Contact us for special arrangements.

## Driving License Translation Service

Drivers from Switzerland, Germany, France, Belgium, Monaco, and Taiwan **cannot use a standard IDP** in Japan. They need an official JAF license translation.

🚗 **[JDLTC — Japan Driver's License Translation Center](https://drive-japan-license.com/)**
- Apply online from anywhere in the world — no need to be in Japan
- Express processing available (as fast as 48 hours)
- PDF delivered by email — print and drive on arrival
- Operated by VanTrip Japan
